# Ruby Gillis

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c35 P0](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0000), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v1 c35 P0](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0000), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Ruby is a very handsome, showy young lady with large, bright-blue eyes and a brilliant complexion. She has long, lovely golden hair worn in braids. She also possesses a plump, showy figure.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)_

## Personality

Ruby is cheerful, good-tempered, and enjoys the pleasant things of life frankly. She laughs a great deal and is easily frightened or nervous, such as when pretending to act dead. She prefers social fun over bothering about books and studies when not required.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P13](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0013), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003)_

## Traits

- Nervous and easily frightened  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001), [v1 c28 P13](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0013)</sub>
- Cheerful and good-tempered  <sub>[v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001)</sub>
- Dislikes overly intellectual conversation  <sub>[v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003)</sub>

## Goals

- To teach for two years before getting married

## History

Ruby grew up in Avonlea as a schoolmate and friend of Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews. On a midsummer afternoon, she gathered with the girls by the pond to play-act Tennyson's poem of Elaine, though she was terrified of lying down in the boat to pretend to be dead. Later, she attended Queen's Academy along with her Avonlea classmates, where she was recognized as the handsomest girl of the year. During her Friday evening walks home from the train, Gilbert Blythe nearly always walked with her and carried her satchel.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001), [v1 c28 P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)_

## Quotes

> I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright.  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>
